title.en: Evaluated Blender mesh as the runtime geometry contract

summary: Treat Blender's editable base mesh and modifier stack as source data, then deliberately export either the evaluated result or an authored fallback that glTF can carry.
objective: The imported asset matches the approved evaluated silhouette and topology budget, with no expectation that Three.js will reproduce Blender modifiers.
applies_when: A Blender mesh depends on bevel, mirror, subdivision, array, boolean, geometry-generating, or deformation modifiers before glTF export.
intent_signals: should I apply modifiers before GLB
example_prompts: Export a non-destructive Blender product model to Three.js without losing its Boolean and bevel silhouette.
Audit why an Array-and-Mirror environment prop has different geometry in the browser.
negative_signals: Rebuild every Blender modifier procedurally in Three.js
Assume viewport wire counts equal exported vertex counts
not_for: Live procedural modeling in the browser, which needs an explicit runtime generator.
Exact CAD exchange or editable Blender modifier transport.

principles: A modifier stack is Blender authoring state. glTF receives geometry attributes and node transforms, not the editable modifier operations that produced them.
Stack order is part of the shape: approve the evaluated result in the same order that export calculates it, and preserve the un-applied source file separately.
Runtime cost is measured on exported primitives. Triangulation, flat edges, UV seams and other discontinuities can increase the delivered vertex count beyond the base mesh count.
implementation: Duplicate or version the delivery object, keep the editable source intact, and evaluate the stack top to bottom. Resolve warnings and inspect silhouette, holes, thin surfaces and shading before export.

Choose one boundary: enable Apply Modifiers in Blender's glTF exporter for a fixed mesh result, or manually apply only after preserving a source copy. Convert curves or other unsupported authoring types to an approved mesh snapshot.
Triangulate deterministically when triangle layout affects deformation, bakes or review. Record exported triangle, vertex, primitive and material-slot counts rather than quoting the edit mesh.
Load the GLB with GLTFLoader. Three.js owns draw materials, culling, disposal and optional runtime deformation; it does not own or replay Blender's modifier stack.
Keep a named comparison fixture with a Boolean opening, mirrored asymmetric marker and rounded edge. Compare its imported silhouette and counts against the approved export.
observable_checks: The browser silhouette, openings and mirrored side match the evaluated Blender object from front, side and grazing views.
The delivery report lists imported triangle and vertex counts; an increase caused by triangulation or attribute seams is explained rather than mistaken for duplicate objects.
Disabling Apply Modifiers changes the fixture in the predicted way, proving which boundary owns evaluation.

creative_affordances: Keep a high-detail Blender source and export separate close, medium and far evaluated meshes.
A runtime generator can replace a modifier only when that procedural behavior is an explicit product feature.
known_limits: Exporter behavior can change; verify the installed Blender version before production delivery.
This record does not prescribe a universal polygon budget.
Authored reusable guidance; no export, import or runtime artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender modifiers are non-destructive, their stack is calculated from top to bottom, and applying makes a result permanent; Blender's glTF exporter can export the evaluated mesh after all modifiers, automatically triangulates quads and n-gons, and may split vertices at discontinuous UVs or flat-shaded edges.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 authoring and exporter behavior; it does not guarantee identical behavior in another Blender or exporter version.
